finalText: Overfitting occurs when a machine learning model learns the noise and random fluctuations in the training data rather than the underlying patterns that generalize to new examples. This typically happens when the model is too complex relative to the amount of training data, causing it to memorize specific data points instead of capturing broader relationships. The result is excellent performance on training data but poor predictive accuracy on unseen test data, which can be mitigated through regularization, cross-validation, or reducing model complexity.
